correctness.rationale: An exact greedy-embedding lemma gives first-position plus positive cyclic jumps. First symbols and jump sequences bijectively label distinct words; summing bounded compositions over two threshold intervals proves the profile. A formal coefficient identity proves the rational series. Cumulative distributions of threshold multisets prove phase dominance, and least thresholds plus unit jumps give sharp LCS lengths and 1/2 multiplicities. Direct independently generated subsequence sets matched 1,820 formula entries across 280 profiles, plus symmetry, LCS and order checks. No finite test is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recent literature identifies deletion-ball intersections as the exact ambiguity measure for sequence reconstruction. For the natural all-symbol cyclic permutation family, the theorem determines every alphabet/length/phase/radius value and a strict phase-distance order; the coefficientwise comparison and longest-word multiplicity are structural facts not provided by a generic LCS algorithm or scalar upper bound. It supplies reusable exact benchmarks for q-ary reconstruction and doubly periodic comparison, rather than an unmotivated finite parameter table.
